facts.description: Al'Akir is the most intelligent and cunning among the Elemental Lords. Master of the skies and storms, he commands the winds to bring either destruction or protection at his will. His followers admire his subtlety, viewing him as a strategist capable of both dominating and safeguarding the heavens. Though his actions may seem unpredictable, they are always driven by his unwavering desire to reign supreme over the skies.

Auranism is the faith in the Windlords, great elemental beings that claim dominion over the endless skies of Azeroth. Followers seek to emulate the wisdom and intelligence of their gods, raising great spires as symbols of their devotion. They invoke the winds and seek the guidance of the Windlords in their decisions, that they may one day free their masters from imprisonment in Skywall and restore their rule over the aerial currents.

facts.description: Upon exposure to the ideas of the Forgotten Shadow, many scientifically-minded individuals come to question whether the forces of the universe deserve the reverence of divinity at all. For some, the magical science of Alchemy proves the key to bending the forces of the universe to one's will. For if nothing is sacred, anything can be a tool; and any tool can be a weapon...

Desperate times have led many who once walked the path of Light to question whether it alone can bring salvation to the benighted realms of Azeroth. This is especially true for those who live in lands ravaged by the Damned and the depredations of the Fel. For many of these lost souls, the logical assumption is that the Tyrism must be balanced with the forces of the Shadow for peace to return. Some of these seak a cure to the curse of Undeath; others a potent weapon to fight the Fel. Whatever their motives be, these often outcast individuals have banded together around the rediscovered teachings of Forgotten Shadow.

facts.description: The mortal followers of the Red Dragonflight are fierce defenders of life and the order of nature. They believe that the duty of safeguarding all life and administering justice entrusted to the red dragons by the Aspect of Life constitues the truest claim on Divinity through the power of the flame. Their faith emphasizes righteousness and empathy, as they strive to protect the vulnerable from the strong. For the followers of the Red Dragonflight, life is a precious gift that must be cherished and safeguarded. For the Dragons themselves, their belief in and loyalty to the Queen Mother is synonymous with their mission to protect life and justice in keeping with the sacred mission passed down by the Titans of old.

The divine mantle of Azeroth's protectorship was passed down first from the Titans to the Keepers, then from the Keepers to the Dragons. For the Dragons themselves, Draconism exemplifies their wc race's promise to uphold their sacred duty; yet many lesser creatures have also devoted themselves to serving these mighty beings with religious fervor. When dragons empower these mortals, they transform into dragonspawn and drakonid, drawing their strength from the dragons they serve.

facts.description: A sect of Avians who worship Anzu, the Raven God. Contrasting Rukhmar's love of the sun and sky, Anzu prefers the cool of the shade and the peace of the twilight hours, where he can be solitary in peaceful contemplation. He is the ancient enemy of Sethe, who cursed him long ago to be broken and flightless, along with many of his creature_arakkoa_corrupted followers.
A group of faiths aroused among the creature_arakkoa_corrupted of Draenor consisting of four Avian gods: Rukhmar, Anzu, Sethe and Terokk, the greatest of the arakkoan kings now worshipped as a god.

facts.description: Rejecting the concept of heresy, the Argentists believe that all life has the right to exist and be free from suffering. As staunch warriors, they see it as their sacred duty to purge and protect the world of evil forces. While the Light is their guide, they seek to understand and interpret it in a personal way, rejecting any fundamentalist conception.

Tyrism is a faith centered around the Light, which is believed to guide and protect its adherents. The religion emphasizes the importance of justice and compassion, and its followers seek to uphold these values in all aspects of their lives. Remembering Tyr's sacrifice, adherents fight evil and banish darkness.

facts.description: The August Celestials are four Wild Gods of Pandaria. The Celestials built temples to train monks in their respective styles after the pandaren revolution. facts.description: Azshara was the powerful queen of the Highborne. Such was her talent and beauty, that she was widely beloved and venerated. Blinded by her hubris and lust for power, she was tricked by Sargeras into kickstarting the War of the Ancients which led to the Sundering. Not all hope was lost though, as she made a deal with N’Zoth to be saved in exchanged for becoming a queen on his side once the Black Empire is established. As such, her and her followers were transformed into the creature_naga.

A congregation of cults worshipping the Old Gods, parasitic, eldritch horrors spawned by the Void Lords to corrupt the cosmos. During the Ordering of Azeroth, the Titans imprisoned them deep beneath the earth to halt their corruption and allow the world to flourish. Their adherents are nihilistic, serving only the Void’s endless hunger.

facts.description: The Black Harvest was born from the quest for potent magic. The group of warlocks that formed the council had the goal of harnessing the power of demons and fel without becoming slaves to them. They came to the conclusion that through collaboration, newfound powers would be uncovered and shared, thus bolstering their knowledge and might. A strict tenet was established: any betrayer or weakling would be cast out by their peers, their soul banished forever. Though the Black Harvest is driven by a thirst for power, they possesses the resilience to not be entirely consumed by it, unlike other warlocks.
Fel Followers believe that Chaos is the natural order of things. They are masters of Fel magic, created as a result of the mutual destruction of the Light and the Void.

facts.description: Bent on destroying all life in the universe, Sargeras is seen as one of the greatest threats to creation, and in a smaller sense, Azeroth. At his beck and call during his burning crusade across the Great Beyond is a loyal, fel-infused army of demons, the burning legion, ready to carry out the destruction Sargeras desires. Followers of the Dark Titan are only capable of cruelty and deceit, as they chase any chance to bring about the extinguishment of life.
Doombringers believe that the universe is corrupted and that there's no way to save it. It must burn. Every living being must die.

facts.description: A pantheon of Loa founded by the creature_vulpera. Ariwo, a fox loa, is the main Loa of this pantheon. He taught his children to stick together and be kind to each other because he felt that it was the only way to survive. Despite the fact that Ariwo disappeared thousands of years ago, his followers still honor his covenants.

Loa is the name given by trolls to beings they worship such as the Wild Gods or spirits. This large group of cults originated in ancient times when the first mortals started encountering magical creatures and deifying them.

facts.description: Shal'danalism consists of the traditions and reverence of the Nightwell; its followers depend on and are changed by the Nightwell's power. A relic of pre-Sundering wc elven wo family culture, Shal'danalists favor the arcane philosophy of their past as they preserve and evolve their ways in unending isolation from the outside world.
For the most part, the secular followers of this philosophy regard Arcane magic as a manifestation of divinity in the world, bestowed on them by ancestors and abstract deities.

facts.description: The mostly secular followers of the Belorism see the Sun as a source of Arcane magic on Azeroth. In their darkest hour, they may pray to the Sun as if it was a living deity.

facts.description: Who would have thought that even such a simple thing as a candle could become a symbol of faith? Kobolds, that dwell in underground tunnels and spend their lives mining, primarily for gold, are sure that the candle is wise. And this is not surprising, because in the condition of darkness it is the candle that helps the Candlists to survive. Perhaps the Candle protects them from something else too.
A wide group of beliefs built around the deification of natural phenomena, spirits and elementals.

facts.description: A pantheon of Loa founded by the tortollans. Torga, a turtle Loa, is the main Loa of this pantheon. He is a wise and benevolent Loa, and his followers frequently undertake pilgrimages to him to hear his stories.

Loa is the name given by trolls to beings they worship such as the Wild Gods or spirits. This large group of cults originated in ancient times when the first mortals started encountering magical creatures and deifying them.

facts.description: Fortunism is an ideology based around the goal of making a profit. Fortunists find themselves to be pragmatic, placing their faith in gold and their own abilities to hoard it. They dismiss insubstantial concepts such as shamanism and religion, preferring power and influence in measurable quantities that they can touch, see, and spend as their aspirations demand.
A broad group of secular philosophies. Secularists don't worship any god because they see no point in following a religion.

facts.description: When the lich_king lost his power, a lot of death knights were released from his grasp. Not having a home to return to, they banded together to defeat him. Although they broke free from the lich_king's control, they could not return back to their old faiths due to their nature. As such they've developed their own worldviews to accomodate their situation. Their centre are the Knights of the Ebon Blade, an organization of freed scourge members dedicated to protecting their world.
A group of numerous cults praising Death. Necroists master necromantic magic, allowing them to make contact with the Other Side.

facts.description: In the face of the ever-looming darkness, our faithful rise in indomitable union to repel the shadowy forces intent on swallowing the world whole. Thus, while acknowledging the diversity of beliefs, we stand firm that our struggle is the most righteous, and we are prepared to do whatever it takes to triumph over the darkness.

facts.description: Upon manifesting free will, the compulsion is strong to feel cursed by undeath and immediately seek a way to return to life. For many, the only possible answer can be found in the arcane. Calling on these potent forces, these so called Echoseekers use wild magicks to attempt to pull their life essence back from the void. Unfortunately, experimenting with these forces can cause magic addiction.

Desperate times have led many who once walked the path of Light to question whether it alone can bring salvation to the benighted realms of Azeroth. This is especially true for those who live in lands ravaged by the Damned and the depredations of the Fel. For many of these lost souls, the logical assumption is that the Tyrism must be balanced with the forces of the Shadow for peace to return. Some of these seak a cure to the curse of Undeath; others a potent weapon to fight the Fel. Whatever their motives be, these often outcast individuals have banded together around the rediscovered teachings of Forgotten Shadow.

facts.description: Also called the Faithless, the Atal'rohki, translatable into destroyers of faith, are those who turned their backs on their serpent loa, Sethraliss. The heretics turned away from the path of peace to become machines of war, forcefully using the divine essence of Sethraliss to fulfill their interests and their destiny.

The Apostates are those who have chosen to turn against their former loas, the deities revered by their people, for various reasons. Their impious acts are considered difficult to forgive, but they have the possibility to gather and support each other, forming a community of individuals who share a desire for freedom or power from their ancient gods.

facts.description: A pantheon of Loa founded by the Farraki trolls. Balancing on the brink of heresy, they perform bloody rituals reminiscent of those practiced by Hakkari. Their main mystical Loa, Mueh'zala, is unknown to other pantheons.

Loa is the name given by trolls to beings they worship such as the Wild Gods or spirits. This large group of cults originated in ancient times when the first mortals started encountering magical creatures and deifying them.

facts.description: A heretical group of shadow magic practitioners, the Forgotten believe that dark energy practitioners are just as vital to the survival of life and reality as wielders of the Light. The cult preaches balance, mandating that shadow priests must never forget the dangers of being corrupted by the dark energies they manipulate... For it is often difficult to find one's way back to the shadow from the deep reaches of the darkness.

Desperate times have led many who once walked the path of Light to question whether it alone can bring salvation to the benighted realms of Azeroth. This is especially true for those who live in lands ravaged by the Damned and the depredations of the Fel. For many of these lost souls, the logical assumption is that the Tyrism must be balanced with the forces of the Shadow for peace to return. Some of these seak a cure to the curse of Undeath; others a potent weapon to fight the Fel. Whatever their motives be, these often outcast individuals have banded together around the rediscovered teachings of Forgotten Shadow.

facts.description: Those who worship water deities perform rituals to commune with the sea and its powers, venerating both the water and the mighty beings within it. The pantheon is ever-shifting, adapting as new creatures are encountered. Even a strong shark or swift fish may become a living symbol, and as they die or move on, the faith changes to embrace new symbols from the ocean.

This is the traditional religion of the Murlocs, where shamans emphasize the power of the waves and the spirits within. While the rituals are often disorganized, the intent behind the worship holds the greatest significance. Outsiders usually find these beliefs hard to grasp, as each tribe has its own unique interpretation.

facts.description: G’huun is the god of blood and rot, a being born not of the Void like his brethren, but created inadvertently by the Titans in their attempt to solve the problem of the Old Gods. Unlike his kin, G'huun scorns technology, drawing his followers into a primitive state. Those touched by his corruption are seen as his beloved children, bound to him by blood and decay.

A congregation of cults worshipping the Old Gods, parasitic, eldritch horrors spawned by the Void Lords to corrupt the cosmos. During the Ordering of Azeroth, the Titans imprisoned them deep beneath the earth to halt their corruption and allow the world to flourish. Their adherents are nihilistic, serving only the Void’s endless hunger.

facts.description: Glowbound is a religion that emerged after the release of gas during the siege of Gnomeregan. It combines traditional Gnomeregan beliefs with the worship of gas and radiation, which its followers see as a source of transformation and enlightenment.
Followers of Radiationism believe that radiation and toxic gases are divine forces of transformation and evolution. They see exposure to the radiation as a way to progress.

facts.description: The Oracles are a faction of several friendly creature_gorloc tribes that inhabit Sholazar Basin. They see themselves as guardians of the titan technology that remains in the area, though they don't really have an understanding of the artifacts they are guarding.

This is the traditional religion of the Murlocs, where shamans emphasize the power of the waves and the spirits within. While the rituals are often disorganized, the intent behind the worship holds the greatest significance. Outsiders usually find these beliefs hard to grasp, as each tribe has its own unique interpretation.

facts.description: A pantheon of Loa founded by the Gurubashi trolls. The concept of death occupies a significant place in this pantheon together with Bwonsamdi, the Loa of Death. Gur'atali pay special attention to interactions with the body of the deceased like ritual cannibalism.

facts.description: Helya, the matriarch of Helheim, which is the underworld of the creature_vrykul who have fallen and failed to ascended to the Halls of Valor, was a Watcher who assisted Odyn in imprisoning elementals into the Elemental Plane. When she rebelled against Odyn, she became the first spectral Val'kyr. She would later create a champion who would bear Odyns warswords of the Valajar, which Helya stole from Odyn. This champion would slay many so that their souls would serve in Helheim. She would also create the Helarjar, a holy order mocking Odyn's Valarjar. The Kvaldir of Helya would also be responsible for murdering the dishonorable and unworthy, taking them to Helheim.

facts.description: Originating from the magical city of Dalaran, the Kirin Tor hope to instil a sense of respect and wonder for the arcane arts into the new generation of mage hopefuls, all while delving deeper into the secrets of Magic itself. While some of these mages worship magic as a whole, those from Lordaeron still venerate the Light, albeit with some arcane twists.

Tyrism is a faith centered around the Light, which is believed to guide and protect its adherents. The religion emphasizes the importance of justice and compassion, and its followers seek to uphold these values in all aspects of their lives. Remembering Tyr's sacrifice, adherents fight evil and banish darkness.

facts.description: A zealous branch of naaru teachings, the Lightbound doctrine drives its adherents to spread the Light’s influence universally, converting unbelievers by any means—even force, if deemed necessary. They see the Light as the path to true peace and justice and will stop at nothing to eliminate what they perceive as obstacles to its unity.

The Light manifests itself as a golden, shining light energy. The naaru, enigmatic beings composed of shards of fractured Light, taught the way of the Light to the creature_draenei and other enlightened wc races. As opposed to others who came to the Light on their own, the Naaru's teachings guide lesser beings toward purity through virtues of Faith, Courage, and Heart.

facts.description: The followers of the Blue Dragonflight revere the Blue Dragons as majestic guardians of the arcane and the keepers of magic. They believe that the wise Aspect of Magic granted the Blue Dragons the highest claim on Divinity by entrusting them with protection of the boundless magical energies of Azeroth. Their faith emphasizes understanding and responsibly wielding the power of the arcane for the greater good. The Blue Dragons themselves draw their power from the Nexus, where the leylines converge. For these mysterious and often aloof beings, their duty to maintain the flow of magic and catalog all knowledge is a sacred duty to the ancient Titans.

The divine mantle of Azeroth's protectorship was passed down first from the Titans to the Keepers, then from the Keepers to the Dragons. For the Dragons themselves, Draconism exemplifies their wc race's promise to uphold their sacred duty; yet many lesser creatures have also devoted themselves to serving these mighty beings with religious fervor. When dragons empower these mortals, they transform into dragonspawn and drakonid, drawing their strength from the dragons they serve.

facts.description: Born among craft guilds, Masons strongly opposed the Church. They reject superstition and dogma such as the unshakable moral authority of priests or the sacred figure of the king, defending freedom, equality and fraternity under the eye of the Supreme Being.

Tyrism is a faith centered around the Light, which is believed to guide and protect its adherents. The religion emphasizes the importance of justice and compassion, and its followers seek to uphold these values in all aspects of their lives. Remembering Tyr's sacrifice, adherents fight evil and banish darkness.

facts.description: The followers of the Black Dragonflight are powerful protectors and keepers of balance, believing their wise Aspect of Earth entrusts black dragons with safeguarding Azeroth and preserving its balance. They uphold values of order and protection, defending against chaos and destruction. They're intimately connected with the earth's power and believe in protecting Azeroth at all costs, using their strength and wisdom to maintain balance. However, corruption has cast a shadow on their noble mission. Despite this, uncorrupted black dragons serve as a beacon of hope for their mission's potential redemption.

The divine mantle of Azeroth's protectorship was passed down first from the Titans to the Keepers, then from the Keepers to the Dragons. For the Dragons themselves, Draconism exemplifies their wc race's promise to uphold their sacred duty; yet many lesser creatures have also devoted themselves to serving these mighty beings with religious fervor. When dragons empower these mortals, they transform into dragonspawn and drakonid, drawing their strength from the dragons they serve.

facts.description: Neptulon, Lord of the Waters, is worshiped by his followers as both the guardian of oceans and marine life, and the ruthless judge of mortals. Unlike his eternal foe, the Lord of Fire, Neptulon can display moments of cordiality and even benevolence toward mortals. Yet, any who dare to defy his will or stir his wrath will face cataclysms of unimaginable devastation.

The waters cover the vast majority of Azeroth, and thus the Aquelians proclaim the rightful sovereignty of the Waterlords over this immense aquatic realm. They seek ways to free their masters from their imprisonment by the ancient Titans; to restore their legitimate power over the world's oceans and rule unchallenged. Through rituals, the followers honor and appease the waters, believing that their gods' will is expressed through both the fury and the calm of the tides.

facts.description: Of all the Dragons, the Bronze Dragonflight is most poorly understood, and rightly so. Their domain, which they view as a sacred mission entrusted to them by the Aspect of Time, is the safeguarding of chronological and causal order and the integrity of the underlying mechanics of the universe. This puts the Bronze Dragons far beyond the understanding of even the most intelligent mortals, despite being broadly seen as the friendliest and most convivial with lesser beings on the rare occasion they are able to meet one. Thus, mortal followers of the Bronze Dragonflight take their inscrutable utterances and mysterious doings as proof of their ultimate claim on Divinity through the ancient Titans. Because of their poor understanding of their living deities, mortal followers of the Bronze Dragonflight are strong believers in fate and predestination, seeing themselves as being at the mercy of an inscrutable cosmos.

The divine mantle of Azeroth's protectorship was passed down first from the Titans to the Keepers, then from the Keepers to the Dragons. For the Dragons themselves, Draconism exemplifies their wc race's promise to uphold their sacred duty; yet many lesser creatures have also devoted themselves to serving these mighty beings with religious fervor. When dragons empower these mortals, they transform into dragonspawn and drakonid, drawing their strength from the dragons they serve.

facts.description: Ordos, once a shaman, was promised divinity by the Firelords and sacrificed himself to the great flame. Transformed into the demigod of fire, his flesh is now eternally seared, putting him in endless agony. In their reverence, the Ordon fire keepers ritualistically set themselves ablaze to emulate the ascension of Ordos, and cast enchantments and prayers to ease his pain.

Following the teachings of the Firelords, Ignans believe themselves to be the Sons of the Living Flame, the ultimate force of purification and destruction. They are devotees of the firelords, who they seek to free from imprisonment in the Firelands by the ancient Titans and bring annihilation to their mortal enemies. The faithful follow the path of the Flame through acts of extreme devotion, believing that only the Lord of Flame can bring true purity.

facts.description: When the first humans first set sail, they soon spread out to build their kingdoms. Some of them though prefered to instead continue sailing across the sea, revering its creatures deep within. Many of these people took up the habit of sea raiding, commonly known as piracy. Although they are widely disliked due to this, their free and unchained lifestyle was attractive to many on the edges of society who sought wealth and freedom.

The waters cover the vast majority of Azeroth, and thus the Aquelians proclaim the rightful sovereignty of the Waterlords over this immense aquatic realm. They seek ways to free their masters from their imprisonment by the ancient Titans; to restore their legitimate power over the world's oceans and rule unchallenged. Through rituals, the followers honor and appease the waters, believing that their gods' will is expressed through both the fury and the calm of the tides.

facts.description: The faith in lesser known elementals and spirits of the world is called Fetishism. Fetishistic beliefs encompass faiths closely guarded by their peoples. Rituals, wards, and other simplistic practices are employed in worship to their patrons. Worshippers desire some sort of balance with the natural world which binds these primitive beliefs together categorically. This category of faith only differs from other shamanistic faiths by the amount of known information. As further information is uncovered and compiled by explorers, the amount of primitive shamanistic beliefs in Azeroth decreases.
A wide group of beliefs built around the deification of natural phenomena, spirits and elementals.

facts.description: Fire is inherently destructive and violent, and Ragnaros, the Firelord, embodies this absolute power. Living in both fear and reverence, his followers submit to his will through the Majordomo of the Firelands as the sacred intercessor of the Firelord. They believe that only Ragnaros’ flame can bring true purification, and each act of devotion is an attempt to earn the favor of their merciless master.

Following the teachings of the Firelords, Ignans believe themselves to be the Sons of the Living Flame, the ultimate force of purification and destruction. They are devotees of the firelords, who they seek to free from imprisonment in the Firelands by the ancient Titans and bring annihilation to their mortal enemies. The faithful follow the path of the Flame through acts of extreme devotion, believing that only the Lord of Flame can bring true purity.

facts.description: A branch of Avians who worship Rukhmar, the Sun Goddess. After the god Anzu faded into darkness, Rukhmar created the creature_arakkoa_corrupted to represent a fusion of her grace and Anzu's cunning. As the mother of the creature_arakkoa_corrupted, Rukhmar is considered to be their main and most traditional diety. Those who venerate her are believed to reunite with the mother in the skies after their passing.
A group of faiths aroused among the creature_arakkoa_corrupted of Draenor consisting of four Avian gods: Rukhmar, Anzu, Sethe and Terokk, the greatest of the arakkoan kings now worshipped as a god.

facts.description: An orthodox school of theology that holds that Noor has created every moment in time, but that humans have free will to choose between good — what the Light has commanded — and evil — what the Light forbids.

Dar al-Noor is the belief that emphasizes the oneness of the Light and its physical presence in the universe with the stars as revealed by the prophets. Noorists strive to purify their souls and conduct themselves with temperance, justice, and servitude to the Light.

facts.description: Born in despair, Scarletism is a heretical and militant offshoot of the Church that believes unholy creatures were sent to punish humanity for its sins and impiety. They strongly reject all other religions and believe that the unholy creatures and infidels must be purged by a cleansing flame.

Tyrism is a faith centered around the Light, which is believed to guide and protect its adherents. The religion emphasizes the importance of justice and compassion, and its followers seek to uphold these values in all aspects of their lives. Remembering Tyr's sacrifice, adherents fight evil and banish darkness.

facts.description: A sect of Avians who worship Sethe, the Dead God. He was slain by Anzu and Rukhmar, but before his death, Sethe created the Curse, causing many creature_arakkoa_corrupted, as well as Anzu himself, to become flightless. Seen as an evil god by other Avians, Sethekk consider the Curse as a gift, a part of Sethe's divinity granted to his followers.
A group of faiths aroused among the creature_arakkoa_corrupted of Draenor consisting of four Avian gods: Rukhmar, Anzu, Sethe and Terokk, the greatest of the arakkoan kings now worshipped as a god.

facts.description: The Suntouched are a specific branch of Titan worshippers that originated in Uldum as a primary sect of Amathet creature_tolvir. They pride themselves on protecting the works of the Titans and rely on solar magic to smite their enemies. Due to their fanatical nature, they see entities that are not affiliated with the Titans as tainted by the Void's influence, and therefore unworthy of existence.

A group of religions dedicated to the Titans, a wc race of colossal, planet-sized cosmic beings, composed of arcane magic and the primordial matter. They shaped and gave order to Azeroth before continuing their cosmic journey, leaving their followers to await Azeroth's world soul's awakening.

facts.description: Theradras, the only daughter of Therazane, is a powerful earth elemental and the mother of the centaurs of Kalimdor. When her progeny, the creature_centaur, killed their father Zaetar over his disgust at their appearance, Theradras fell to rage bordering on insanity. Having retreated to Maraudon, she now bargains with dark forces to usurp her mother and spreads corruption across the land through her malformed children.

The Terrans worship the Stonelords, masters of Deepholm and guardians of the World Pillar that supports Azeroth. While Therazane embodies stability and protection, others like Theradras represent the more destructive aspects of the earth. Through their rituals, the faithful honor the enduring power of the earth, aware that creation and destruction can lie in the hands of their gods.

facts.description: Unlike the other Elemental Lords, Therazane is a more peaceful deity, preferring to protect her children rather than engage in unnecessary conflicts. Her followers revere her as a maternal figure, embodying the nurturing aspects of the earth. They reject needless violence and strive to follow her example, promoting preservation, stability, and patience.

The Terrans worship the Stonelords, masters of Deepholm and guardians of the World Pillar that supports Azeroth. While Therazane embodies stability and protection, others like Theradras represent the more destructive aspects of the earth. Through their rituals, the faithful honor the enduring power of the earth, aware that creation and destruction can lie in the hands of their gods.

facts.description: Many spirits of the fallen Drust have been banished into an offshoot plane within the Emerald Nightmare that they later named Thros, where they cultivated a potent form of death magic with bastardized druidic elements. This form of magic resulted from numerous attempts to bewitch the souls of fallen Drust into constructs to use against creature_human settlers. Following this, the Throsic form of necromancy prefers binding the souls of the dead into durable constructs, while the traditional form of corpse reanimation is rarer. Its influence towards the wildlife and the living is usually perpetuated by the local witch covens. The most loyal of Throsian witches can also ascend into Matrons, an incorporeal banshee-like creature, through a ritualistic act of slitting their own throat in ultimate devotion to their horrific masters.
A group of numerous cults praising Death. Necroists master necromantic magic, allowing them to make contact with the Other Side.

facts.description: Lei Shen, the thunder king, was a legendary creature_mogu emperor and demigod that single-handedly defeated the despondent creature_titan_keeper Ra-den within the Thundering Mountain. Lei Shen subsequently stole both Ra-den's power and a fraction of Aman’Thul's power, giving him immense mastery over the storms whose power could rival many of the cosmos' powerful beings. He proceeded to use his newfound power to conquer ancient Pandaria and forge an empire of the Mogu, with their mandate being the continued work of the Makers after their supposed demise at the hands of the Dark Titan. Highly meritocratic, the followers of the Shenism believe that they are the only ones worthy to rule and uphold the ancient titan legacy in Azeroth.

A group of religions dedicated to the Titans, a wc race of colossal, planet-sized cosmic beings, composed of arcane magic and the primordial matter. They shaped and gave order to Azeroth before continuing their cosmic journey, leaving their followers to await Azeroth's world soul's awakening.

facts.description: The Tidemother is a being worshipped by many sailors and those whose lives depend on favorable sea winds. Many Tirani look to the seas for guidance the same way others look to the Light, but the tidesages, the priests of the Tidemother, have a much deeper connection with the water. Long have the tidesages listened to the sea to guide their ships and their people, hearing gentle whispers imperceptible to most.

The waters cover the vast majority of Azeroth, and thus the Aquelians proclaim the rightful sovereignty of the Waterlords over this immense aquatic realm. They seek ways to free their masters from their imprisonment by the ancient Titans; to restore their legitimate power over the world's oceans and rule unchallenged. Through rituals, the followers honor and appease the waters, believing that their gods' will is expressed through both the fury and the calm of the tides.

facts.description: A shamanistic primitive faith of worshipping salamanders. Tales of the monstrous beasts tell they are descendants of mighty dragons, and seeing the reptilians with their fiery breath as weapons and an omnivorous appetite it might be true. Making their lairs underground in caves, they have dominated their surrounding environment. Sentient dwellers abiding in these harsh environments venerate the salamanders as the masters of the food chain and strive to live and learn from them to achieve greater strength and mastery of the land.
A wide group of beliefs built around the deification of natural phenomena, spirits and elementals.

facts.description: The Oachani worship a small pantheon of deities or spirits such as Tayutka, Karkut, Issliruk, and Oacha'noa. In addition, the Oachani carve massive stone heads that allow them to communicate with their ancestors. Each head houses the specific spirit of an elder which acts as both home and body, thereafter referred to as stone elders. A Oachani shaman uses a set of ritual items to perform a ceremony, in which they recite a chant in a strange language to guide an ancestor's spirit to their rightful statue.
A wide group of beliefs built around the deification of natural phenomena, spirits and elementals.

facts.description: The Twilight's Hammer Cult is an apocalyptic and nihilistic sect fanatically devoted to the Old Gods. Their worldview rejects any notion of meaning in the universe, believing that the inevitable fate of existence is to be consumed by darkness. Violent and destructive, they seek to hasten the collapse of the world to fulfill their dark prophecy. Some even believe they are destined to rule alongside their masters after the prophesied Hour of Twilight.

A congregation of cults worshipping the Old Gods, parasitic, eldritch horrors spawned by the Void Lords to corrupt the cosmos. During the Ordering of Azeroth, the Titans imprisoned them deep beneath the earth to halt their corruption and allow the world to flourish. Their adherents are nihilistic, serving only the Void’s endless hunger.

facts.description: Ursinism is a tradition practiced by favoring balance of the wild things and the natural world. The twin Ancient Guardians Ursol and Ursoc receive veneration mostly from Ursol's descendants, the furbolgs. Furbolgs attuned to nature grow into druids and shamans, following Ursol's woven path. Ursoc's path, on the other hand, is saturated with blood. Following it, warriors and hunters learn the ferocity of nature.
A group of beliefs deifying nature. The Druidists worship countless spirits and gods living in the deep forests, jungles, lakes and oceans of Azeroth.

facts.description: Teachings of the naaru known as K'ure, as revealed to the Prophet Velen. Inspired by K'ure’s vision, Velen led the creature_draenei exodus from Argus, saving them from Sargeras' curse. Pursued across the cosmos, the Velenei lead lives of unwavering virtue according to the Naaric values of Faith, Courage, and Heart; protecting the souls of their dead from the grasping claws of demons and the gaping maw of the Void.

The Light manifests itself as a golden, shining light energy. The naaru, enigmatic beings composed of shards of fractured Light, taught the way of the Light to the creature_draenei and other enlightened wc races. As opposed to others who came to the Light on their own, the Naaru's teachings guide lesser beings toward purity through virtues of Faith, Courage, and Heart.

facts.description: The powers of the Fel can be tempting to all living beings in the universe, but there are those who use it as a tool to fight the evil that lurks throughout creation, rather than for personal gain or destruction. Although these individuals can often be found guilty of similar crimes as those of power-hungry warlocks and demons, they see any suffering inflicted as means to a greater end, an end greater than themselves and their sacrifices. Though more realistically benevolent than most demons and warlocks, society will seek to reject them and their cruel, yet effective, methods nonetheless.
Fel Followers believe that Chaos is the natural order of things. They are masters of Fel magic, created as a result of the mutual destruction of the Light and the Void.

facts.description: While dangerous, Void magic can be carefully used for the benefit of its users and their allies. Some Void practitioners have devoted their lives to the study and use of the Void for good, such as the denizens of the Telogrus Rift, although there are some that are much more morally ambiguous than their peers, such as the K'areshi ethereals. Nevertheless, they can all enjoy the benefits of the Void without interference from the Old Gods, but still risk being corrupted by the malevolent whispers.

Despite the fact that many think that Void Followers are nothing more than crazy maniacs, this is far from the truth. They learn to control Void magic without defiling their minds. Unlike Tyrists, they're more tolerant and don't believe in only one way.

facts.description: Waterspeaking is an ancient belief that originated in Pandaria before the Great Sundering, that allows its followers to commune with the land through rituals involving river water. The only ones to maintained the long tradition of waterspeaking long after the mists have concealed the continent were the fish-people known as creature_jinyu. Over time, the wisest of their people learned to commune with the waters of the river and listen for the future and news it would bring.

The waters cover the vast majority of Azeroth, and thus the Aquelians proclaim the rightful sovereignty of the Waterlords over this immense aquatic realm. They seek ways to free their masters from their imprisonment by the ancient Titans; to restore their legitimate power over the world's oceans and rule unchallenged. Through rituals, the followers honor and appease the waters, believing that their gods' will is expressed through both the fury and the calm of the tides.

facts.description: The mortal followers of the Green Dragonflight revere the ancient Draconic guardians of nature, champions of balance and growth. The Aspect of Nature entrusted the Green Dragons with the duty of protecting the natural world and maintaining the delicate equilibrium between all living things, and these mortals believe that this constitutes the highest claim on Divinity. For the Dragons themselves, their faith lies in the divine compact they made with the Titans and Keepers. It is manifested through their connection with the sacred Emerald Dream, a realm where the essence of nature resides in the combined subconscious of all living things. While the Green Dragons themselves spend most of their lives asleep, their true power manifests in the Emerald Dream and they often communicate to chosen followers from beyond the veil of sleep.

The divine mantle of Azeroth's protectorship was passed down first from the Titans to the Keepers, then from the Keepers to the Dragons. For the Dragons themselves, Draconism exemplifies their wc race's promise to uphold their sacred duty; yet many lesser creatures have also devoted themselves to serving these mighty beings with religious fervor. When dragons empower these mortals, they transform into dragonspawn and drakonid, drawing their strength from the dragons they serve.

facts.description: Y’Shaarj was the most powerful and wicked of the Old Gods, known as the "Beast of Seven Heads." Each head represented one of his aspects: Anger, Hatred, Violence, Fear, Doubt, Despair, and Pride. When Aman’Thul tore Y’Shaarj from Azeroth, the world itself was wounded. With his final breath, he unleashed the Sha, malevolent echoes of his dark essence.

A congregation of cults worshipping the Old Gods, parasitic, eldritch horrors spawned by the Void Lords to corrupt the cosmos. During the Ordering of Azeroth, the Titans imprisoned them deep beneath the earth to halt their corruption and allow the world to flourish. Their adherents are nihilistic, serving only the Void’s endless hunger.

facts.description: A pantheon of Loa founded by the Zandalari trolls. This is one of the most ancient pantheons. However, it is renowned for its adaptability. Zan'atali respect all other Loa in order to maintain friendly ties with other Loa sects.

Loa is the name given by trolls to beings they worship such as the Wild Gods or spirits. This large group of cults originated in ancient times when the first mortals started encountering magical creatures and deifying them.
